data.segment_title: Preview/Introduction Tom Brokaw (Democratic National Convention in Boston)

data.segment_description:
(Boston: Tom Brokaw) Tonight’s agenda at the Democratic National Convention in Boston reviewed. 
 (Convention floor: Brian Williams) The message the Democrats hope to convey at the convention featured; details given of Senator John Kerry’s focus on national security following the release of the 9/11 Commission’s report; scenes shown of vice presidential candidate Senator John Edwards arriving in Boston. [KERRY – calls for immediate implementation of the 9/11 Commission’s recommendations and an extension of their mandate.] [Illinois senate candidate Barack OBAMA – says he would like to restore a sense of hope about our politics.] [Former presidential candidate Howard DEAN – comments on blaming President Bush for everything that’s wrong with this country.] [Last night, former President Bill CLINTON – says strength & wisdom are not opposing values.] 
 (Boston: Tom Brokaw) Report introduced. 
 (Democratic National Convention: Andrea Mitchell) The behind-the-scenes work of Democratic Party operatives to be sure their message is picked up by the media featured; scenes shown from the Democratic “war room”; details given of the strategy to build on Clinton’s words last night. [Kerry foreign policy advisor Jamie RUBIN&#134&#134- comments on Kerry’s call to continue the work of the 9/11 Commission.] [Kerry campaign communications director Stephanie CUTTER†, Senator Joseph BIDEN – reinforce the message of Kerry’s strength & wisdom.] [Kerry pollster Mark MELMAN††- says Americans are concerned about the job Bush has done since September 11.] 
 (Boston: Tom Brokaw) Report introduced. 
 (Camp Pendleton, California: David Gregory) The administration’s response to Democrats’ attacks on Bush’s national security policies featured; scenes shown from Vice President Dick Cheney’s campaign tour of the Northwest while Bush is on vacation. [At Camp Pendleton in California, CHENEY – speaks about the war on terror.] [Political analyst Stuart ROTHENBERG†- says the Republicans feel they have to be out there every day.] [Democratic pollster Geoffrey GARIN†- comments on Cheney’s loss of credibility due to the war in Iraq.]
(Boston: Tom Brokaw) Charges against the Texas-based Muslim charity Holy Land Foundation for supporting terrorists linked to Hamas reported.

(Boston: Tom Brokaw) Report introduced.   (Washington: Pete Williams) The pressure on the administration & Congress to act on the 9/11 Commission’s recommendations immediately featured; details given of  decision to begin Congressional hearings this week and of the administration’s steps toward tightened security. [Senator Susan COLLINS†- says we have a lot of work to do to produce legislation that can pass this fall.] [9/11 victim’s father Lee IELPI††- comments on the threat of an attack between now & the end of the year.] [Representative Anthony WEINER†- says we should not hesitate.] [Senator Chuck HAGEL††- warns against making changes too quickly.]   (Boston: Tom Brokaw) Statistics on sales of the 9/11 Commission report and Website hits cited.

data.segment_description:
(Boston: Tom Brokaw) The views of Stanford University’s Dr. Irving Weissman†† on the controversy over stem cell research presented in his own words. [WEISSMAN&nbsp- expresses his view that we could treat ALS {Lou Gehrig’s disease} if stem cell research was allowed & funded by the government & not criminalized by the Senate; states we could make cell lines that represent each & every human disease; says we are stuck with an ideological ban; states those who vote for a ban are responsible for the lives that are lost.] Tonight’s speech regarding stem cell research by former President Ronald Reagan’s son Ron Reagan at the Democratic National Convention noted. 
 (New York: Robert Bazell) The status of stem cell research today examined; details given about the potential & limitations of stem cells. [Alzheimer’s disease caregiver Jane STEIN††- says hopefully Nancy Reagan will be able to push it.] [Diabetes patient Rich GURWITZ††- comments on his successful treatment.] [Diabetes Research Institute Dr. Juan Dominguez BENDALA††- says it’s possible we'll be using human embryonic stem cells to treat type 1 diabetes in the near future.] [Columbia University Dr. Michael SHELANSKI††- explains why stem cells probably won’t help Alzheimer’s patients.]
